features.method: OpenStreetMap way 171900954 (building=yes, man_made=telescope, name=H.E.S.S., telescope:diameter=12m), a closed 7-node polygon used verbatim, no simplification. features.method: Quadrilateral whose four vertices are the centroids (hepgraph.atlas.geo.centroid) of the four corner-telescope footprints, OpenStreetMap ways 171900951 (north), 171900954 (east), 171900955 (south), 171900956 (west), joined N-E-S-W. Replaces the previous square, which had been placed on the array's published coordinate and so carried that coordinate's 200 m uncertainty. The perimeter check compares this OSM-derived quadrilateral with the published 120 m side (480 m perimeter): an independent test, because the OSM positions were not fitted to it.
features.name: H.E.S.S. CT1-CT4 telescope square (120 m side, diagonal north-south)

provenance.locator: centroids of OSM way/171900951, way/171900954, way/171900955, way/171900956 as of the 2026-10-25T10:35:43Z OSM API extract; H.E.S.S. Telescopes page 'Arrangement of the telescopes'
provenance.note: Confidence 'derived' per contract: a derived shape is derived, even with a passing check.
provenance.quote: The initial four H.E.S.S. telescopes (Phase I) are arranged in form of a square with 120 m side length ... The diagonal of the square is oriented north-south.

features.method: OpenStreetMap way 171900953 (building=yes, man_made=telescope, name='H.E.S.S. 2'), a closed 7-node polygon used verbatim, no simplification. Replaces the earlier point that re-used the array's published coordinate. Four distance checks measure its centroid to each corner telescope's centroid against 120 m / sqrt(2), the centre-to-corner distance of the published 120 m square with CT5 at its centre.
features.name: H.E.S.S. CT5 telescope (28 m, centre of the array)

provenance.note: OpenStreetMap trace (rank 11) caps confidence at approximate. The footprint's span is 29.7 m against a 24 m x 32 m reflector (28 m circular equivalent, Puhlhofer 2024), so it is the telescope structure, not a surveyed mirror outline.
provenance.quote: an single huge dish with about 600 m2 mirror area was added at the center of the array

provenance.note: Land-use polygon, not a fence or a surveyed boundary; no official figure to check against.

summary.plain: The H.E.S.S. gamma-ray telescope array on Farm Gollschau in the Khomas Highland of Namibia: four 12 m telescopes on a 120 m square, the 28 m CT5 dish at its centre, the control building and the residence.
